name: IRONLIMB GeckoFrame Digi Climb Series 9
description:
The GeckoFrame Series 9 is Ironlimb's answer to urban vertical access, combining a standard digitigrade load-transfer chassis with van der Waals adhesion toe pads — four articulated synthetic digits per foot, each surfaced in micro-setae polymer that generates dry adhesion on glass, concrete, painted steel, and most architectural polymers. The reverse-knee geometry shifts the wearer's center of gravity forward, which Ironlimb's engineers found naturally optimizes for wall-surface contact posture. Adhesion toggles on and off via neural command, disengaging in under 80ms.

GeckoFrames are bought by building access specialists — some legitimate (tower maintenance, window washing rigs), most not. Urban infiltrators, trespassers, and the small criminal economy of people who get into places they shouldn't be have made the Series 9 a known quantity to building security firms, who now actively scan for the thermal signature of the toe pads. The digitigrade silhouette alone is enough to trigger elevated alerts in most Tier 3+ corporate lobbies.
installation_requirements: Full bilateral hip disarticulation, standard neural socket, Ironlimb-certified installation preferred but third-party capable; adhesion pad calibration session required post-surgery
rejection_risk: Low — Ironlimb uses proven industrial-grade interface hardware with wide neural compatibility tolerance
maintenance: Micro-setae pad replacement every 4-6 months depending on use surface; joint inspection annually; adhesion toggle neural calibration check every 6 months
specifications: {"adhesion_surface_types": ["glass", "concrete", "painted steel", "architectural polymer", "brick"], "digits_per_foot": 4, "adhesion_toggle_response_ms": 80, "max_supported_load_on_vertical_kg": 140, "setae_material": "micro-polymer van der Waals array", "frame_material": "hardened steel composite", "weight_per_leg_kg": 6.2, "max_climb_angle_degrees": 105, "power_source": "subcutaneous cell pack", "adhesion_recharge_cycle_hours": 12}
side_effects: Unintentional adhesion activation during stress or sleep — users have woken stuck to metal bed frames
Forward-shifted center of gravity causes stumbling on standard flat surfaces during early adaptation period
Toe pad micro-setae accumulate environmental debris and require regular cleaning to maintain adhesion efficiency
Security profiling is near-universal — GeckoFrames are on watch lists maintained by most major Tier 3+ building security systems
cultural_context: The GeckoFrame's association with breaking-and-entering is so established that wearing them in public is effectively a declaration of intent in the eyes of most security professionals and law enforcement. Ironlimb technically markets them for industrial access work, but the Restricted classification and the reality of who buys them have fused the product's identity with urban infiltration. Wearers face the standard digitigrade stigma plus an additional layer of presumed criminal purpose.
known_users: Urban infiltrators and corporate espionage operatives
Legitimate tower maintenance and high-rise access workers (small minority)
Burglars and physical security testers who blur that line
Tier 2 scavengers accessing abandoned upper-floor structures in collapsed Mid-Ring zones
story_hooks: A series of impossible-access thefts from Spire towers have left GeckoFrame micro-setae residue — but the registered owner of matching legs has a verified alibi
A building security firm is contracting players to test a new anti-adhesion surface coating — the test involves actually trying to climb their client's tower
A maintenance worker with GeckoFrames found something on the 94th floor of a sealed corporate tower and hasn't been seen since
